{{short description|American statistician}}
'''Krista Jennifer Gile''' is an American statistician known for her research on [[respondent-driven sampling]], on [[exponential random graph models]], and more generally on the statistical behavior of [[social network]]s.{{r|unexpected}} She is an associate professor in the department of mathematics and statistics of the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]].

==Education and career==
Gile grew up in [[Shrewsbury, Vermont]], where her father Richard H. Gile was an engineer and businessman.{{r|profile}}
She graduated in 1998 from the [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]], where she majored in electrical engineering with a minor in sociology.
After earning a master's degree in science and technology studies at [[Virginia Tech]] in 2000, she worked from 2000 to 2003 as Assistant Director of Research at Advocates for Human Potential, Inc.{{r|cv}} In this period, she also continued to take graduate classes, delivered meals for the poor and taught mathematics to underprivileged girls.{{r|unexpected}}

At the suggestion of an amateur rugby teammate and with the encouragement of a sociological theory professor, she returned to graduate school,{{r|unexpected|profile}} studying statistics at the [[University of Washington]], 
where she completed her doctorate in 2008.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''Inference from Partially-Observed Network Data'', was supervised by [[Mark S. Handcock]].{{r|diss}}
After two years as a Postdoctoral Prize Research Fellow at [[Nuffield College, Oxford]], she joined the UMass Amherst faculty in 2010.{{r|cv}}
